title: Check absolute paths directly using relative(), not by pre-normalization
context: The misroute guard was meant to catch when agents record findings/decisions in the wrong checkout (worktree vs. root). A prior fix attempted to handle absolute paths by relativizing them against root before existence checks, but this failed: agents working in a sibling worktree naturally send paths rooted at their own cwd, which relativize to "../…" against root and get silently dropped — reintroducing the exact #54 bypass the guard exists to prevent. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Replace pre-normalization (guardFiles, correctionScopeHint) with a path-aware existence check (existsUnder) that handles both relative and absolute entries directly: relative paths join onto the directory as before; absolute paths are checked AS THEMSELVES, confirmed via relative() to actually fall under that directory's own tree. An absolute path existing under a sibling worktree's tree is now direct positive evidence for that worktree, not a heuristic requiring normalization against root.
consequences: Correctly identifies misroutes where agents send worktree-rooted absolute paths
Absolute paths are now evidence of which specific directory contains them, not normalized away
Removed correctionScopeHint and guardFiles public API surface (reduced unnecessary exports)
Test cases updated to reflect realistic agent behavior (joining against worktree, not root)
alternatives_rejected: Pre-relativizing all paths against root before checking (fails for sibling worktree absolute paths)
Naive join(root, absolutePath) checks (produces nonexistent concatenated paths)
Complex heuristics to infer worktree membership from absolute path shape
